title: The Two Sun-Faced Kites
skyStory: The slim Leo crescent, sixteen percent lit, drapes itself across the sky like a cat on a warm windowsill. Tonight it is in the mood for tricks. The sun has left it a box of coincidences to play with, and it is batting them around the solar system like ping pong balls. Saturn is trying to keep score. Saturn has already lost count.

reading: Sunday morning, a yellow kite with a grinning sun painted on it will be tangled in a tree near the cabin road, its tail fluttering like it is waving at you. Nobody is around to claim it. It looks thrilled with itself. You will laugh. You will take a photo.

By afternoon Nancy will send a photo of a kite stuck in a tree by the shore. Yellow. Grinning sun. Same crooked tail. Don't even scream. Leo is ruled by the Sun, and [[The Sun]] from your spread is apparently flying itself around the province now. Stop earning joy. It is literally hanging in the trees.
joel.mission: Fly something today, a paper plane, a leaf or a kite, and send Nancy a three-second video of it in the air.
joel.omen: Anything caught in a tree and smiling. Somebody is thinking about you at the same moment you think of them.

reading: The Wood Rat spots it first: a yellow kite snagged high in a birch by the water, its painted sun beaming down like it owns the beach. You know immediately it needs to be documented. You do not know yet that Joel is staring at its twin.

When the photos match, call it out. DES of the season, possibly the year. Then let the rest of your Sunday be soft and unhurried. The shore is quiet, the light is low, and the first real cold of autumn arrives in the evening breeze. Wave at any kite you see today, just in case it is a relative.
nancy.mission: Draw a little sun face on something today, a sticky note or a foggy window, and leave it where someone will find it.
nancy.omen: Two matching objects in two different places. The universe is sewing a quilt with your days.

together.text: Name the two kites and write the story of how they escaped, in four sentences, with a happy ending where they meet again at the solstice. ΔΕΣ has been entered in the logbook under Airborne Synchronicities, page three.

game.intro: Don't even scream: two matching sun-faced kites, one sky. Two of your sky facts are true, one drifted in from fiction.
game.prompt: Three things you saw up in the sky this month: clouds, birds or something stranger.
